intro: General and operations managers build coordination, people management and problem-solving skills that nearly every leadership role needs. Of the 25 careers below, Project Management Specialists, Administrative Services Managers and First-Line Supervisors of Non-Retail Sales Workers all match at 90%.
why_it_works: Running operations means setting priorities, managing staff and fixing problems across departments at once. O*NET rates coordination at 3.88 out of 5 for this job, so project, logistics and specialty management roles rank high. Most of these moves keep your level and change the area you lead, such as sales, production or finance. Project management uses the same planning with a clearer scope. The main gaps are technical ones, such as systems analysis and programming.
tips: Pick an industry you already know, since specialty managers in production, logistics or health care are often hired for sector knowledge.
Get a project management certification if you want a formal title for the planning you already do.
Build one technical skill, such as data analysis, to close the systems analysis gap the top matches show.

faq.q: What jobs can general and operations managers move into?
faq.a: The closest matches are Project Management Specialists (90%), Administrative Services Managers (90%) and First-Line Supervisors of Non-Retail Sales Workers (90%), based on O*NET 31.0. Information Technology Project Managers (89%) and Sales Managers (89%) are also close, so most moves keep you at the same level.

faq.q: Which careers pay more than operations management?
faq.a: 15 of the 25 matches pay more than the $105,770 median for general and operations managers. Marketing Managers earn $166,790 (+58%), Financial Managers earn $166,570 (+57%) and Compensation and Benefits Managers earn $149,230 (+41%), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do operations managers need another degree to switch?
faq.a: Not for the roles on this page: all 25 matches usually need no more education than an operations manager has, based on O*NET Job Zones. Some specialty roles, such as financial manager, still expect deep experience in that area, so plan for a bridge role.

faq.q: What is the next step up from operations manager?
faq.a: Within top management, the nearest role is Chief Executives, with an 87% match by skills. Chief Sustainability Officers (70%) is a newer path for managers who want to lead environmental programs. Both build on the coordination and people skills you already use.
